anomalies.observed: The isolated CAN transceivers U10 and U11 have both their primary-side ground pin (GND1) and secondary-side ground pin (GND2) connected to the same GND net.
anomalies.expected: For an isolated CAN transceiver, GND1 and GND2 must be on separate, isolated ground nets (e.g., board GND and an isolated CAN/bus ground) to preserve galvanic isolation between the CM4/CAN-controller side and the CAN bus.

evidence.quote: GND [High Power] : ... U10.4(GND1,power_in) U10.5(GND2,power_in) U11.4(GND1,power_in) U11.5(GND2,power_in)
Interface_CAN_LIN:ISO1050DUB | Isolated CAN Transceiver, SOP-8 | pins: ... 4=GND1(power_in) 5=GND2(power_in)
two isolated CAN buses (`CAN0`, `CAN1`), each driven by its own MCP2515 SPI CAN controller (`U8`, `U9`) through an isolated CAN transceiver (`U11`/companion)

anomalies.impact: The isolation barrier of both CAN interfaces is shorted; the CAN bus and motor-controller-side ground are not isolated from the CM4 ground, defeating the intended isolated CAN buses and allowing ground loops/noise/fault currents across the isolation boundary.

parsed.summary: The design files show a clear anomaly: the isolated CAN transceivers U10 and U11 have GND1 and GND2 tied to the same GND net, shorting the isolation barrier and contradicting the specified isolated CAN buses.
